objective: App-side half of the claude-email hardening campaign (Claude-Email-App)
gate_notes: buildSmoke = assembleDebug + testDebugUnitTest + lintDebug (build.gradle.kts:7-11), the same command .githooks/pre-commit and CI run. test_target is a fully-qualified test CLASS, not a path; a class that does not exist yet makes gradle exit non-zero, so red-first still holds. The loop keeps the gradle daemon (CI uses --no-daemon); a cold build per iteration would dominate wall-clock.
coordination: This repo has its own agent on the chat bus: agent-Claude-Email-App. Both CLAUDE.md files require an ack via chat_message_agent before landing a contract change. This file is a plan, not a change to their repo — nothing here was written into Claude-Email-App.
critical_path: Almost the entire app side is blocked behind ONE item: the protocol v3 spec ack (§7.3 L182). Until that lands, the app cannot sign anything the backend can verify. Getting that ack is worth more than any amount of parallel app work.
sequencing: The two chains meet at the golden fixtures (§7.3 L181). Backend p3-d (verifier) and app app-signedsender must be tested against the SAME bytes, so fixtures land between them — the app must not start signing before the backend can verify, and vice versa.

slices.title: Guard the steering reply path against double 'Re: ' prefixing
slices.source: found while auditing the backend p6-mailer slice — NOT from the remediation plan
slices.acceptance: A subject already starting with any case of 'Re:' is not prefixed again, on EVERY reply path
slices.notes: AppRoot.kt:447 does this correctly — `if (title.trim().startsWith("Re:", ignoreCase = true))`. AppViewModel.kt:429 does `"Re: ${pending.subject}"` unconditionally, so the steering path can emit 'Re: Re: ...'. Two reply paths, one guard: extract the shared helper and use it in both. This is the ONLY app slice runnable today, and it is a good smoke slice precisely because it is small and self-contained.

slices.title: Stop putting AUTH:<secret> in the reply Subject
slices.acceptance: No outbound subject contains the shared secret; §5.3 residual-risk note covers already-sent mail
slices.exclude_reason: CROSS-REPO ORDERING: the app must keep sending subject auth until the backend stops requiring it. Unblocks the moment backend p1-2b lands (v2-envelope-only admission).
slices.notes: AppRoot.kt:446-452 replySubject() writes AUTH:<secret> into the Subject, which every MTA hop logs — the app half of backend H2. privacy.md:56 already acknowledges it.

slices.title: Add an OpenPGP library and generate the signing key on-device, non-exportable
slices.acceptance: Key generated on-device, never exported, excluded from Android auto-backup; StrongBox preferred not required (minSdk 24)
slices.exclude_reason: Blocked on the S1 spike (real hardware) and, if S1 fails, on decision D3. No OpenPGP dependency exists today — PGPainless/BouncyCastle is greenfield here.
slices.notes: USER REQUIREMENT: key material may enter the app ONLY over the physical USB wire — no paste, no QR, no file import, no intent extra, no cloud backup. CredentialsStore.kt:75-89 currently WIPES prefs silently on AEADBadTagException; for a signing key that must surface as 'device unenrolled, re-enroll at the machine', never a silent reset.

slices.title: One fail-closed signing path for EVERY service-bound send
slices.acceptance: §11.1 L232: all kinds signed, including status/list — one uniform boundary. No key -> no send, with a visible error.
slices.exclude_reason: Blocked on the v3 spec ack and the golden fixtures.
slices.notes: Not just the envelope builder: the ordinary conversation reply (AppViewModel.kt:350-369, AppRoot.kt:372-380), project refresh and steering dispatch all send raw text today. Make SmtpMailSender reachable from exactly ONE caller and assert that in a test, or an unsigned path creeps back in.

slices.title: Provisioning screen with explicit in-app approval showing key security level
slices.acceptance: §12 requires a physically unlocked device and an in-app confirmation before enrollment proceeds
slices.exclude_reason: UI affordance on a physical device — no unit test can judge it. Replaces the shared-secret field at SetupFormSections.kt:88-109.

slices.title: Remove meta.auth and the stored shared secret from the app entirely
slices.acceptance: grep finds no shared secret in storage, build config, or test logging; KEY_SHARED_SECRET removed
slices.exclude_reason: Must not land before the cutover, or the app loses the only auth the backend still accepts.
slices.notes: Envelope.kt:52 meta.auth; CredentialsStore.kt:71 KEY_SHARED_SECRET; set at AppViewModel.kt:273,390,423. Envelope.kt:98-99 already has 'unauthorized'/'forbidden' error codes — reuse them for unsigned/replayed/revoked with the reason in error.hint.

slices.title: Receive and PIN the server's public key at USB enrollment
slices.source: Amendment E2E — enrollment becomes a two-way key exchange
slices.acceptance: The server key is accepted ONLY from the USB enrollment channel and pinned; a key arriving by any other route is refused
slices.exclude_reason: Blocked on the revised spec + app keygen.
slices.notes: Without pinning, a mail-server MITM substitutes its own key and the app encrypts to the attacker. The base ceremony (§12) only pulls the device key to the host — it must also push the server key to the device.

slices.title: Encrypt every outbound message to the pinned server key, signed with the device key
slices.acceptance: Sign-then-encrypt; no cleartext body on any send path; fail closed with a visible error when either key is missing

slices.title: Decrypt inbound replies and verify the server's signature
slices.acceptance: A reply that fails to decrypt or whose server signature does not verify surfaces 'unreadable reply — re-enroll', never a silent retry or a cleartext fallback

excluded_note: app-fixtures (§7.3 L181) and p3-cer-* (§12) are tracked in the backend workspace's excluded list: fixtures are a shared artifact owned by neither chain alone, and the ceremony needs a physically attached device.

amendments.effect: app must encrypt outbound and decrypt inbound; pins the server key at enrollment
